---
title: "Matching Methods for Multilevel Data in Education Research"
subtitle: "A practical guide and illustration of approaches in R"
---

**SREE 2026 workshop** · Baltimore · Wednesday, September 23, 2026 · Laurel AB, 9:30 a.m. · 2 hours

**Instructors:** Jordan Rickles (UCLA) and Alberto Guzman-Alvarez (American Institutes for Research)

**Repository:** <https://github.com/alberto-guzman/multilevel-matching-workshop>. Download the zip from the Code button, or clone it. The repository holds everything on this site, including the data and the checkpoints.

The first hour is a lecture on the ideas. The second hour is hands-on, and we run the R code for two matching designs together, chunk by chunk. The code comes from the handbook *Propensity Score Matching in Multilevel Educational Settings*, with the explanatory text removed so that it runs from top to bottom.

## Schedule

| Time | Activity |
|:------|:---------|
| 9:30 | Foundational concepts, multilevel designs, and the six stages (lecture), then Chapter 4, the data and the R packages |
| 10:20 | *Break* |
| 10:30 | Chapter 5, multisite individual assignment design (MIAD) |
| 11:12 | Chapter 6, cluster assignment design (CAD) |
| 11:25 | Close and questions |

## Where to go

- **[Before you come](before_you_come.qmd).** Install R, download the repository, and run the setup script at home, because the wifi in the room may be slow. Start here.
- **[Slides](slides.qmd).** Jordan's lecture slides and Alberto's short deck for the hands-on portion.
- **[Ch5: MIAD](05_miad.qmd)** and **[Ch6: CAD](06_cad.qmd).** The two pages we run in the room. Each opens with a note on the data and on how we use the page in the session.
- **[Ch7: MCAD](07_mcad.qmd).** The multisite cluster assignment design, which combines the other two. We do not run it in the session, so it is there for you to run at home.
- **[Flowcharts](flowcharts.qmd).** The guiding questions and the options at each stage, for choosing an approach for your own study after the session.

## Feedback and testers

Please tell us what worked and what did not, using the form at <https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/XZpKK1aEmY>. The form also asks whether you would like to test the handbook before it is finalized.
